inputs.text: An Indiana judge has blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice framed the restriction as a burden on religious belief. That turns religious liberty into a weapon against the state’s responsibility to protect unborn life. No one’s freedom is unlimited, and calling abortion access “care” doesn’t erase the moral stakes or the interests of the most vulnerable. The real question is whether the law may uphold a society’s duty to defend life—not whether bodily autonomy should always trump it.
